cur:catacombs-adoration-magi-sarcophagus.summary: The Virgin, veiled and seated, holds up the Child, who stretches out his hands to receive the gifts of three Magi in short tunics and Phrygian caps; a star shines above, and the heads of their camels appear behind them. The Child's eager gesture makes this one of the most tender versions of the scene in early Christian sculpture.
facts: Commons states that the panel comes from a Roman sarcophagus found in the cemetery of Sant'Agnese in Rome.
The camels' heads in the background are a characteristic detail of Roman Epiphany scenes.
